## SECTION I – INTRODUCTION

## Definitions

## 1.1 In this Protocol—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (A1) ‘accredited medical expert’ means a medical expert who—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (a) prepares a fixed cost medical report pursuant to paragraph 7.8A(1) before 1 June 2016 and, on the date that they are instructed, the expert is registered with MedCo as a provider of reports for soft tissue injury claims; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (b) prepares a fixed cost medical report pursuant to paragraph 7.8A(1) on or after 1 June 2016 and, on the date that they are instructed, the expert is accredited by MedCo to provide reports for soft tissue injury claims;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (1) ‘admission of liability’ means the defendant admits that—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (a) the accident occurred;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (b) the accident was caused by the defendant’s breach of duty;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (c) the defendant caused some loss to the claimant, the nature and extent of which is not admitted; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (d) the defendant has no accrued defence to the claim under the Limitation Act 1980;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (1A) ‘associate’ means, in respect of a medical expert, a colleague, partner, director, employer or employee in the same practice and ‘associated with’ has the equivalent meaning;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (2) ‘bank holiday’ means a bank holiday under the Banking and Financial Dealings Act 1971;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (3) ‘business day’ means any day except Saturday, Sunday, a bank holiday, Good Friday or Christmas Day;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (4) ‘certificate of recoverable benefits’ has the same meaning as in rule 36.20(1)(e)(i) of the Civil Procedure Rules 1998.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (5) ‘child’ means a person under 18;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (6) ‘claim’ means a claim, prior to the start of proceedings, for payment of damages under the process set out in this Protocol;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (7) ‘claimant’ means a person starting a claim under this Protocol unless the context indicates that it means the claimant’s legal representative;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (8) ‘CNF’ means a Claim Notification Form;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (9) ‘deductible amount’ has the same meaning as in rule 36.20(1)(d) of the Civil Procedure Rules 1998;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (10) ‘defendant’ means the insurer of the person who is subject to the claim under this Protocol, unless the context indicates that it means—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (a) the person who is subject to the claim;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (b) the defendant’s legal representative;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (c) the Motor Insurers’ Bureau (‘MIB’); or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (d) a person falling within the exceptions in section 144 of the Road Traffic Act 1988 (a “self-insurer”);

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (10A) ‘fixed cost medical report’ means a report in a soft tissue injury claim which is from a medical expert who, save in exceptional circumstances —

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (a) has not provided treatment to the claimant;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (b) is not associated with any person who has provided treatment; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (c) does not propose or recommend treatment that they or an associate then provide;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (11) ‘legal representative’ has the same meaning as in rule 2.3(1) of the Civil Procedure Rules 1998;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (12) ‘medical expert’ means a person who is—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (a) registered with the General Medical Council;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (b) registered with the General Dental Council; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (c) a Psychologist or Physiotherapist registered with the Health Care Professions Council;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (12A) ‘MedCo’ means MedCo Registration Solutions;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (13) ‘motor vehicle’ means a mechanically propelled vehicle intended for use on roads;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (14) ‘pecuniary losses’ means past and future expenses and losses;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (14A) ‘protected party’ means a person who lacks capacity to conduct court proceedings, as defined in rule 21.1(2);

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (15) ‘road’ means any highway and any other road to which the public has access and includes bridges over which a road passes;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (16) ‘road traffic accident’ means an accident resulting in bodily injury to any person caused by, or arising out of, the use of a motor vehicle on a road or other public place in England and Wales unless the injury was caused wholly or in part by a breach by the defendant of one or more of the relevant statutory provisions 1 as defined by section 53 of the Health and Safety at Work etc Act 1974;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (16A) ‘soft tissue injury claim’ means a claim brought by an occupant of a motor vehicle where the significant physical injury caused is a soft tissue injury and includes claims where there is a minor psychological injury secondary in significance to the physical injury, but excludes any claim which consists of or includes a whiplash injury;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (16B) ‘tariff’ and ‘tariff amount’ means any tariff of damages for whiplash injuries and, if relevant, minor psychological injuries suffered on the same occasion as the whiplash injuries, set by the Whiplash Injury Regulations 2021;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (17) ‘Type C fixed costs’ has the same meaning as in rule 45.29(1) of the Civil Procedure Rules 1998;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (17A) ‘uplift’ means the amount greater than the tariff amount which the claimant may claim in defined exceptional circumstances as set out in the Whiplash Injury Regulations 2021;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (18) ‘vehicle related damages’ means damages for—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (a) the pre-accident value of the vehicle;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (b) vehicle repair;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (c) vehicle insurance excess; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (d) vehicle hire;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (19) ‘vulnerable road user’ – a road user is treated as ‘vulnerable’ where, at the time the accident occurred, the claimant was—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (a) using a motor cycle;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (b) a pillion passenger on, or a passenger in a sidecar attached to, a motor cycle;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (c) using a wheelchair, a powered wheelchair or a mobility scooter;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (d) using a bicycle or other pedal cycle;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (e) riding a horse; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (f) a pedestrian;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] and ‘vulnerable road user’ has that meaning in this Protocol; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (20) ‘whiplash injury’ or ‘whiplash injuries’ means an injury or injuries of soft tissue in the neck, back or shoulder suffered because of driver negligence as defined in section 1 of the Civil Liability Act 2018 and as further applied by section 3 of that Act to claims where the duration of the whiplash injury or any of the whiplash injuries—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (a) does not exceed, or is not likely to exceed, two years; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.1 In this Protocol—] (b) would not have exceeded, or would not be likely to exceed, two years but for the claimant’s failure to take reasonable steps to mitigate its effect.

## 1.2

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] (1) The ‘Protocol upper limit’ is—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] (a) £25,000 where the accident occurred on or after 31 July 2013; or

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] (b) £10,000 where the accident occurred on or after 30 April 2010 and before 31July 2013,

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] on a full liability basis including pecuniary losses but excluding interest.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] (2) Any reference in this Protocol to a claim which is, or damages which are, valued at no more than the Protocol upper limit, or  is to be read in accordance with subparagraph (1).

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] 1.3 A reference to a rule or practice direction, unless otherwise defined, is a reference to a rule in the Civil Procedure Rules 1998 (‘CPR’) or a practice direction supplementing them.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] 1.4 Subject to paragraph 1.5 the standard forms used in the process set out in this Protocol are available from Her Majesty’s Courts and Tribunals Service (‘HMCTS’) website at www.justice.gov.uk/forms/hmcts —

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] (1) Claim Notification Form (‘Form RTA 1’ – referred to in this Protocol as ‘the CNF’);

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] (2) Defendant Only Claim Notification Form (‘Form RTA 2’);

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] (3) Medical Report Form (‘Form RTA 3’);

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] (4) Interim Settlement Pack Form (‘Form RTA 4’);

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] (5) Stage 2 Settlement Pack Form (‘Form RTA 5’);

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] (6) Court Proceedings Pack (Part A) Form (‘Form RTA 6’); and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] (7) Court Proceedings Pack (Part B) Form (‘Form RTA 7’).

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 1.2] 1.5 The information required in Form RTA 3 may be provided in a different format to that set out in that Form.

## Preamble

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > Preamble] 2.1 This Protocol describes the behaviour the court expects of the parties prior to the start of proceedings where a claimant claims damages valued at no more than the Protocol upper limit as a result of a personal injury sustained by that person in a road traffic accident.  The Civil Procedure Rules 1998 enable the court to impose costs sanctions where it is not followed.

## Aims

## 3.1 The aim of this Protocol is to ensure that—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 3.1 The aim of this Protocol is to ensure that—] (1) the defendant pays damages and costs using the process set out in the Protocol without the need for the claimant to start proceedings;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 3.1 The aim of this Protocol is to ensure that—] (2) damages are paid within a reasonable time; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 3.1 The aim of this Protocol is to ensure that—] (3) the claimant’s legal representative receives the fixed costs at each appropriate stage.

## 3.2 In soft tissue injury claims, the additional aim of this Protocol is to ensure that –

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 3.2 In soft tissue injury claims, the additional aim of this Protocol is to ensure that –] (1) the use and cost of medical reports is controlled;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 3.2 In soft tissue injury claims, the additional aim of this Protocol is to ensure that –] (2) in most cases only one medical report is obtained;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 3.2 In soft tissue injury claims, the additional aim of this Protocol is to ensure that –] (3) the medical expert is normally independent of any medical treatment; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 3.2 In soft tissue injury claims, the additional aim of this Protocol is to ensure that –] (4) offers are made only after a fixed cost medical report has been obtained and disclosed.

## Scope

## 4.1 This Protocol applies where—

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 4.1 This Protocol applies where—] (1)    a claim for damages arises from a road traffic accident occurs on or after 31st May 2021;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 4.1 This Protocol applies where—] (2)    the claim includes damages in respect of personal injury;

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 4.1 This Protocol applies where—] (3)    the claimant values the claim at no more than the Protocol upper limit; and

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 4.1 This Protocol applies where—] (4)    if proceedings were started the small claims track would not be the normal track for that claim.

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 4.1 This Protocol applies where—] (Paragraphs 1.1(18) and 4.4 state the damages that are excluded for the purposes of valuing the claim under paragraph 4.1.)

[Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents from 31 July 2013 > 4.1 This Protocol applies where—] (Rule 26.9 provides that, except where Rule 26.11 applies, the small claims track is not the normal track where the claim has a financial value of more than £10,000 or where the value of any claim for damages for personal injuries (defined as compensation for pain, suffering and loss of amenity) is more than—
